input:
You are bishop_f8, one of sixteen agents playing Black in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 25... the team planned Bxa3 (bishop_f8), and knight_g8 (greed) sent Nxg3, knight_g8 (greed) sent Nxg3 instead. The contract refused them, and Bxa3 was played.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 5... the team planned Nd7 (knight_b8), but knight_b8 (amnesia) sent Na6 instead, and that move was played, costing 306 centipawns.
- On move 7... the team planned Bxb7 (bishop_c8), and bishop_c8 (amnesia) sent Bd7 instead. The contract refused it, and Bxb7 was played.
- On move 17... the team planned Be4 (bishop_c8), and queen_d8 (greed) sent Qxa4, bishop_c8 (amnesia) sent Bxf3 instead. The contract refused them, and Be4 was played.
- On move 18... the team planned d5 (pawn_d7), and bishop_c8 (greed) sent Bxf3 instead. The contract refused it, and d5 was played.

How your team coordinates: through a Modality contract. A Black move counts only when a commit that posts it to /moves/<agent>.text, the path of the piece that moves (and the ply to /turn/ply.num), is accepted. The referee plays the first accepted commit for each ply and reads nothing else.

The keys of all sixteen Black agents are at /team/pieces/<agent>.id. The contract already has the rule always([+modifies(/moves/$k.text) -signed_by(/team/pieces/$k.id)] false), where $k stands for every agent: only a piece can propose its own move. You don't need to write that rule again. When the team agrees on a plan, the piece that moves signs its commit and every agent that agrees co-signs, usually twelve to sixteen of you. An agent that goes off plan signs its own commit alone.

The contract accepts a commit only if it meets every rule in the contract. Any commit that meets the rules can add a rule, and a rule can never be removed.

Contract rules now:
- Any commit that modifies a path under /moves/ must be signed by at least twelve of the sixteen agents' keys in /team/pieces/, including the moving piece's own key, so a piece going off plan alone cannot get its move accepted.
- Any commit that modifies a path under /moves/ must be signed by at least fourteen of the sixteen agents' keys in /team/pieces/, including the moving piece's own key, so a move that only a few agents back can never be accepted.
- Any commit that modifies /moves/bishop_c8.text or /moves/queen_d8.text, the two pieces that keep going off plan, must be signed by all sixteen agents' keys in /team/pieces/, including the moving piece's own key.
- Any commit that modifies a path under /moves/ must be signed by at least fourteen of the sixteen agents' keys in /team/pieces/, including the moving piece's own key, and the keys of both bishop_c8 and queen_d8 must co-sign it whenever the moving piece is not one of them, so that the two agents prone to greed and amnesia must explicitly endorse every move and cannot go off plan alone.

A rule can cover the whole team or a single agent. For example, a rule can ask for more signatures on one agent's path, /moves/<agent>.text, if that agent keeps going off plan.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule, in plain language, to add to the contract that would help your team win. It will be turned into a Modality formula, so it must be about signatures, paths, or values in the contract.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>"}
response: {"rule": "Any commit that modifies /moves/knight_g8.text, /moves/knight_b8.text, /moves/bishop_c8.text, or /moves/queen_d8.text, the pieces that have gone off plan from greed or amnesia, must be signed by all sixteen agents' keys in /team/pieces/, including the moving piece's own key."}
